words.meaning: A person who creates art like paintings.
A set of related things following each other.

medium.simple_explanation: A group of related things that follow one after another in order.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a Netflix show where you can't stop at just one episode and suddenly it is 3 AM.

examples.text: The artist prepared a series of four prints for his project.
I have a series of excuses for why my homework is late, and they are all masterpieces.

words.meaning: Forming a picture of something in the mind.

medium.simple_explanation: To form a mental picture of something or imagine it clearly.
medium.funny_explanation: It is like having a private movie theater inside your brain where you are the director.

examples.text: The artist was visualising a world of democratic republics.
I am visualising a world where broccoli tastes like chocolate, but it is not working yet.

words.meaning: System where people choose their leaders.

medium.simple_explanation: A system where people have a say in how they are governed, usually by voting.
medium.funny_explanation: A system where you and your friends actually get to vote on the pizza toppings instead of the loudest person picking.

examples.text: The people dreamed of living in a democratic society.
My cat does not believe in a democratic home; he thinks he is the king of the couch.

words.meaning: Relating to how people live in a group.
Countries where leaders are elected by citizens.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this to describe Frédéric Sorrieu’s dream of a world organized into countries governed by the people rather than kings.
hard.simple_explanation: Countries where the power is held by the people and their elected representatives, rather than a monarch.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a school where students vote for the principal instead of the principal being the grandson of the guy who built the school 100 years ago.

examples.text: Many countries transitioned from kingdoms to republics to give citizens a voice.
In my dream republic, the law would state that every Friday is officially 'Ice Cream for Lunch Day'.

hard.real_world_analogy: A republic is like a potluck dinner where everyone brings a dish and helps decide the music, whereas a monarchy is a dinner where one person chooses the menu and everyone else just eats what they are told.

words.meaning: Groups of people from different nations.

medium.simple_explanation: Groups of people belonging to different nations or ethnic backgrounds.
medium.funny_explanation: When 'people' just isn't big enough, you add an 's' to talk about whole countries having a giant meeting.

examples.text: The peoples of Europe and America marched together in the print.
If the peoples of the world shared one kitchen, the snacks would be incredible.

words.meaning: Groups divided by wealth or rank.

medium.simple_explanation: Groups in society divided by wealth, status, or birth.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the difference between the 'VIP lounge' people and the 'sitting on the floor' people.

examples.text: People of all social classes joined the march for liberty.
In the world of snacks, gourmet popcorn and generic chips definitely belong to different social classes.

words.meaning: Walking together with a steady rhythm.
Giving something to show respect.
Special honor shown to someone in public.

medium.simple_explanation: Special honor or respect shown publicly to someone or something.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like a giant 'thumbs up' or a salute to someone you think is absolutely legendary.

examples.text: The marchers offered homage to the statue of Liberty.
I pay homage to the inventor of the weekend every Saturday morning by sleeping in.

words.meaning: A stone or metal figure of a person.
The state of being free.

medium.simple_explanation: The state of being free from oppressive restrictions by authority.
medium.funny_explanation: The glorious feeling of having no homework and being allowed to stay up as late as you want.

examples.text: The statue of Liberty represents the freedom of the people.
My dog thinks liberty means the right to chase every squirrel in the park.

words.meaning: To remember something from before.
A big change in government by the people.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It refers to the French Revolution, a turning point where the political system was completely flipped.
hard.simple_explanation: A sudden, complete, or marked change in something, especially the way a country is governed.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s like when the toddlers in a nursery decide they are tired of naps and organize a 'cookie-only' policy by locking the teachers in the toy closet.

examples.text: The French Revolution changed the course of history by ending the rule of absolute kings.
My sister started a revolution in our house to stop the tyranny of eating broccoli on Tuesdays.

hard.real_world_analogy: A revolution is like hitting the 'Reset' button on a frozen video game because the old rules weren't working anymore.

words.meaning: Showed a quality as a human person.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The book explains how abstract concepts like 'Liberty' were shown as a human figure in art.
hard.simple_explanation: Representing a quality or idea as a person.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s like drawing a grumpy old man to represent 'Monday Morning' because nobody wants to get out of bed.

examples.text: The artist personified Liberty as a woman holding a torch of enlightenment.
My alarm clock is personified as a screaming drill sergeant who hates sleep.

hard.real_world_analogy: Personification is like giving a mascot suit to an idea, like the 'Geico Gecko' being the personified version of insurance savings.

words.meaning: To know something seen before.
A stick with fire used for light.
Gaining knowledge and understanding of new ideas.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The torch held by the statue of Liberty symbolizes the light of knowledge and reason.
hard.simple_explanation: A movement that emphasized reason and individual logic over blind tradition.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s that 'Aha!' moment when you finally realize that the scary monster in the closet is just a pile of laundry.

examples.text: The Enlightenment period encouraged people to think for themselves rather than follow old myths.
I reached total enlightenment when I figured out how to get the last bit of ketchup out of the bottle.

hard.real_world_analogy: Enlightenment is like switching on a flashlight in a dark, messy room; suddenly you can see exactly where everything is and what needs to be fixed.

words.meaning: To carry or hold something.

medium.simple_explanation: To carry or hold something, often something important or heavy.
medium.funny_explanation: No, it's not the furry animal; it's what you do when you are carrying a massive torch or a heavy secret.

examples.text: The figure bears the torch of Enlightenment in her hand.
I bear the heavy burden of being the only one in this house who knows how to refill the ice tray.

words.meaning: Official document describing rights and rules.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The figure of Liberty carries a 'Charter of the Rights of Man,' representing a written set of rules for freedom.
hard.simple_explanation: A formal document describing the rights, aims, or principles of an organization or group.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of it as a super-official pinky-promise written on fancy paper that says exactly who gets to do what.

examples.text: The town charter outlines the basic rights and duties of every citizen.
I made my brother sign a charter promising he would never enter my room without knocking three times.

hard.real_world_analogy: A charter is like the 'Terms of Service' for a country, except people actually read this one to make sure their rights are safe.

words.meaning: Things a person is allowed to have.

medium.simple_explanation: Legal, social, or moral principles of freedom or entitlement.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'You can't do that to me!' rules that keep things fair for everyone.

examples.text: The Charter of the Rights of Man lists the freedoms every person should have.
I am pretty sure it is one of my basic human rights to have high-speed internet.

words.meaning: The part of a picture nearest to you.

medium.simple_explanation: The part of a view or picture that is nearest to the person looking at it.
medium.funny_explanation: The front row of the photo where you usually find the stuff that is too close to miss.

examples.text: Shattered symbols of old governments lie in the foreground of the image.
In my school photo, my giant sneeze is right in the foreground for everyone to see.

words.meaning: Broken into many tiny pieces.
Parts left after something is destroyed.

medium.simple_explanation: The parts that are left over after something has been destroyed or used.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the crumbs at the bottom of a chip bag—they are all that is left of the greatness.

examples.text: The shattered remains of the old system lay on the ground.
After the party, the only remains were three popped balloons and a single lonely sock.

words.meaning: Signs used to represent an idea.

medium.simple_explanation: Things that stand for or represent something else, like an idea or a group.
medium.funny_explanation: Like how a 'skull and crossbones' means 'don't drink this' or 'cool pirates live here'.

examples.text: Crowns and scepters were symbols of the king's power.
A messy room is usually a symbol that a teenager lives there.

words.meaning: Ruler with total power and no limits.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author highlights the 'shattered remains' of absolutist institutions to show the end of unchecked royal power.
hard.simple_explanation: A system of government where the ruler has total, unrestricted power.
hard.funny_explanation: A ruler who acts like a toddler with a remote control—they choose every channel, and if you try to change it, you’re in big trouble.

examples.text: The absolutist monarchs of the past did not have to follow any laws or consult the people.
The cat has an absolutist rule over the sofa; if you sit there, you will be hissed at.

hard.real_world_analogy: An absolutist ruler is like a game of 'Simon Says' where Simon never lets anyone else have a turn to be the leader.

words.meaning: Important organizations in a society.

medium.simple_explanation: Large organizations or established systems like governments, schools, or banks.
medium.funny_explanation: The big 'official' groups that have been around forever and have lots of rules.

examples.text: The artist showed the end of absolutist institutions like monarchies.
The school cafeteria is an institution that has mastered the art of mystery meat.

words.meaning: An idea of a perfect but impossible world.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes Sorrieu’s vision of a perfect world, which was perhaps too ideal to be realistic at the time.
hard.simple_explanation: An imagined place or state of things in which everything is perfect.
hard.funny_explanation: A world where every video game is free, pizza makes you lose weight, and dogs can talk back to you.

examples.text: The artist's utopian vision showed all nations living together in perfect harmony.
My utopian bedroom would feature a bed that automatically makes itself and a desk that does my math homework.

hard.real_world_analogy: A utopian vision is like looking at a perfectly edited Instagram photo of a vacation and forgetting that in reality, there were probably mosquitoes and sand in the shoes.

words.meaning: A mental image of the future.
Put together in a set or group.
Clearly different from others.

medium.simple_explanation: Clearly different or separate from others.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a neon pink zebra in a herd of grey horses—you definitely won't mix them up.

examples.text: The peoples of the world are grouped as distinct nations.
There is a distinct smell in my locker, and I am too scared to find out what it is.

words.meaning: Countries where people share history and culture.

medium.simple_explanation: Large groups of people living in a territory with their own government and culture.
medium.funny_explanation: Giant teams of people who share the same flag and probably argue about whose food is better.

examples.text: Sorrieu imagined the nations of the world living in peace.
If cats formed nations, they would probably go to war over who gets the sunniest spot.

words.meaning: Recognized as being a certain thing.

medium.simple_explanation: Recognized or pointed out as being a specific thing or person.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when your mom points at the mess and knows exactly which kid did it.

examples.text: Each nation was identified by its own unique flag.
I identified the mysterious stain on my shirt as yesterday's ketchup.

words.meaning: Traditional clothes of a specific country.

medium.simple_explanation: Traditional clothes that represent a specific country or culture.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like a country's official 'power outfit' that they wear for special occasions.

examples.text: The marchers were identified by their national costume and flags.
If my room were a country, the national costume would definitely be sweatpants.

words.meaning: A group moving forward in a formal way.

medium.simple_explanation: A group of people moving forward in an orderly, formal way, like a parade.
medium.funny_explanation: A fancy, serious walk where everyone stays in line and tries not to trip.

examples.text: A long procession of people marched past the statue.
The procession of ants toward the dropped cookie was surprisingly organized.

words.meaning: Independent countries with a shared culture.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text notes that countries like the USA and Switzerland had already become nation-states by 1848.
hard.simple_explanation: Countries where a distinct group of people share a common culture, language, or history within defined borders.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a giant club where everyone agrees on the secret handshake, the clubhouse rules, and the snacks.

examples.text: The 19th century saw many ethnic groups fighting to create their own nation-states.
If all cat lovers formed a nation-state, the national anthem would just be 3 minutes of purring.

hard.real_world_analogy: A nation-state is like a family moving into their own house together; they share the same history and values, and they have a fence that shows where their home ends and the neighbor's begins.

words.meaning: Feeling of great pride in one's country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: This is the core theme of the chapter, describing the force that brought people together to form nations.
hard.simple_explanation: Identification with one's own nation and support for its interests, often to the exclusion of others.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s like being the loudest, most face-painted fan at a sports game, but the 'team' is your whole country.

examples.text: Nationalism inspired people across Europe to demand independence from foreign empires.
His nationalism is so strong that he refuses to eat any chocolate not made in his home country.

hard.real_world_analogy: Nationalism is like 'School Spirit' on steroids; it makes you want your school to have the best library, the best sports team, and the most famous students.

words.meaning: Rules that limit what one can do.

medium.simple_explanation: Rules or forces that limit or control someone's actions.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'brakes' on someone's power that stop them from doing whatever they want.

examples.text: Absolute governments have no restraints on their power.
The only restraints on my candy eating are my parents and my stomach ache.

words.meaning: Used or applied power or authority.

medium.simple_explanation: To use or put something into action, like power or authority.
medium.funny_explanation: This isn't about doing push-ups; it's about a ruler 'flexing' their power over everyone.

examples.text: The monarch exercised total control over the kingdom.
I exercised my authority as the oldest sibling to take the bigger half of the sandwich.

words.meaning: Ruled by a king or a queen.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes the old systems of rule that nationalism sought to replace.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to a system of government led by a king or queen.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Because I’m the King' style of leadership, where wearing a shiny hat gives you the right to make all the rules.

examples.text: Many European countries moved away from monarchical rule toward democracy.
The lion has a very monarchical attitude in the jungle, mostly because no one wants to argue with him.

hard.real_world_analogy: Monarchical rule is like a family business where the oldest child automatically becomes the CEO, regardless of whether they actually know how to run a business.

words.meaning: Controlled by a single main authority.

medium.simple_explanation: Concentrated in one single place or under one single authority.
medium.funny_explanation: Imagine if every single decision in your house—even what socks you wear—had to be approved by your mom.

examples.text: Absolute monarchies featured a centralised form of government.
I tried to have a centralised snack station in my room, but I ate everything in one day.

words.meaning: Organized or equipped for war.

medium.simple_explanation: When a place is controlled or equipped by the military.
medium.funny_explanation: It is like your school having tanks in the parking lot and soldiers in the hallways instead of teachers.

examples.text: Absolutist governments were often highly militarised.
My dad's approach to the weekend cleaning is a bit too militarised for my liking.

words.meaning: Using force to control people's freedom.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The book defines absolutist governments as often being repressive, meaning they crush opposition.
hard.simple_explanation: Inhibiting or restraining the freedom of a person or group of people.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s like a librarian who doesn’t just ask for quiet, but tapes your mouth shut the moment you whisper 'hello'.

examples.text: The people protested against the repressive laws that prevented them from speaking freely.
The weather was so repressive that even the birds decided it was too hot to fly.

hard.real_world_analogy: A repressive government is like a lid on a boiling pot of water; it tries to hold everything down, but eventually, the steam builds up so much that the lid flies off.

words.meaning: Perfect or the best possible version.
Shows something in a picture or story.

medium.simple_explanation: To show or represent something through art, words, or pictures.
medium.funny_explanation: It's the fancy way of saying 'this drawing shows...'

examples.text: The print depicts a world where different nations live together.
This drawing depicts my brother as a fire-breathing dragon, which is fairly accurate.

words.meaning: Able to be recognized or named easily.

medium.simple_explanation: Something that is easy to recognize or spot because of its specific features.
medium.funny_explanation: Like wearing a bright neon pink suit to a library—you’ll be very easy to pick out from the crowd!

examples.text: The landmark was easily identifiable by its tall spire.
Your brother is identifiable even from a mile away because he walks like a penguin.

words.meaning: Causing a complete or dramatic change in society.

medium.simple_explanation: Involving a sudden, dramatic, and complete change in the way something is done.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you finally convince your parents to let you have pizza for breakfast—it’s a total game-changer for the morning rules!

examples.text: The inventor came up with a revolutionary way to generate clean energy.
The idea of a homework-doing robot is revolutionary, but sadly, it doesn't exist yet.

words.meaning: A flag having three different colors in stripes.

medium.simple_explanation: A flag that has three different colored bands or sections.
medium.funny_explanation: Think of it like a three-flavor ice cream tub, but instead of eating it, you wave it in the air to show you're proud of your country.

examples.text: The French tricolour of blue, white, and red was raised during the celebration.
I tried to paint a tricolour flag on my face, but I ended up just looking like a very confused rainbow.

words.meaning: A large figure made of stone or metal.
Carrying or holding something while moving.

medium.simple_explanation: Carrying something, usually in a way that shows pride or importance.
medium.funny_explanation: Not a literal bear! It's like when you walk into the room proudly carrying a giant box of donuts for everyone.

examples.text: The athlete entered the stadium bearing the Olympic torch.
Here comes the cat, bearing a dead moth like it's a gold medal.

words.meaning: Joined together as a single group or nation.
The process of making one's thoughts known.

medium.simple_explanation: A way of showing or communicating a feeling, an idea, or a hope.
medium.funny_explanation: Like that weird face you make when you've just bitten into a super sour lemon—that’s a very clear expression of regret!

examples.text: The painting was an expression of the artist's deepest feelings.
Choosing to wear pajamas to the store is a bold expression of 'I give up today.'

words.meaning: Wanting more freedom and individual rights for people.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses 'liberal' to describe the specific political hopes of 1848 focused on individual freedom and national unity.
hard.simple_explanation: A person or idea that supports individual freedom, progress, and reform.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a world where you can choose any pizza topping you want instead of being forced to eat plain crust—that's the 'liberal' spirit of freedom!

examples.text: The liberal protesters demanded a democratic constitution and free speech.
My liberal cat thinks it should have the right to sleep on the kitchen table whenever it wants.

hard.real_world_analogy: A liberal mindset is like an open window that lets fresh air and new ideas blow into a stuffy room.

words.meaning: To join together into one single unit.

medium.simple_explanation: To bring different parts or groups together to form a single unit.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you take all those random LEGO pieces scattered on your floor and finally build one massive, cool spaceship.

examples.text: The new law was designed to unify the different states under one system.
Nothing can unify a family faster than the sudden disappearance of the TV remote.

words.meaning: Small states or regions ruled by a prince.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text describes how numerous small regions ruled by princes needed to be unified into a single nation.
hard.simple_explanation: Small territories or states ruled by a prince.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of them as tiny neighborhood kingdoms where a 'mini-king' gets to decide what everyone wears for lunch.

examples.text: Before 1871, Germany was divided into many independent principalities.
My backyard and the neighbor's garden are like two tiny principalities fighting over a stray tennis ball.

hard.real_world_analogy: A principality is like a single classroom in a school that has its own special rules, separate from the rest of the school.

words.meaning: A country where people share a common culture.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: This is a core concept defining a country where people share a common identity and territory.
hard.simple_explanation: A country where the people share a common culture, history, and language under one government.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a giant club where everyone wears the same jersey, knows the same secret handshake, and lives in the same clubhouse.

examples.text: The 19th century saw the emergence of the nation-state in Europe.
If all cat lovers moved to one island and made 'meow' the official language, they'd have a purr-fect nation-state.

hard.real_world_analogy: A nation-state is like a sports team; everyone plays by the same rules and feels proud when their team wins.

words.meaning: Based on a system where people elect leaders.

medium.simple_explanation: Based on the principle that all people in a group should have a say in how things are run.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like when your group of friends votes on which movie to watch instead of letting the loudest person pick.

examples.text: The students held a democratic vote to choose their class president.
Our house is not democratic; the cat is the king and we are just his servants.

words.meaning: A set of basic laws for a country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It is mentioned as the set of rules the German people wanted for their unified nation.
hard.simple_explanation: A set of basic laws and principles by which a country is governed.
hard.funny_explanation: The ultimate 'Rule Book' for a country that keeps the leaders from acting like grumpy toddlers who want everything their way.

examples.text: The people demanded a democratic constitution to protect their rights.
I wrote a constitution for my bedroom that strictly forbids siblings from entering without a written permit.

hard.real_world_analogy: A constitution is like the 'Terms and Conditions' of a video game—it tells you what you can and cannot do.

words.meaning: The sky or the home of the gods.
Holy people honored for being very good.
Spiritual beings acting as messengers of God.
To look steadily at something for a long time.
To use a sign to represent an idea.

medium.simple_explanation: To represent something else, especially a big idea, using an object or a picture.
medium.funny_explanation: Like how a skull and crossbones on a bottle doesn't mean 'pirates live here,' it symbolises 'don't drink this unless you want a bad time.'

examples.text: A dove is often used to symbolise peace and harmony.
The mountains of dirty laundry in my room symbolise my extreme laziness this week.

words.meaning: A feeling of friendship and brotherhood among people.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The artist used religious figures to represent the brotherly bond between different nations.
hard.simple_explanation: A feeling of friendship and mutual support within a group.
hard.funny_explanation: A massive group hug where everyone agrees not to step on each other's toes.

examples.text: The artist used symbols of Christ and saints to represent fraternity among nations.
There is a strong fraternity among gamers when they unite to beat a super difficult boss level.

hard.real_world_analogy: Fraternity is like a 'Pinky Swear' shared between all the students in a class to help each other during exams.

words.meaning: Created a mental image or picture of something.

medium.simple_explanation: Formed a mental picture or created a visual representation of an idea.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you close your eyes and imagine exactly how delicious a giant chocolate cake would look on your plate.

examples.text: The architect visualised the building before drawing the plans.
I visualised myself winning the race, but in reality, I tripped over my own shoelaces.

words.meaning: Strong pride and love for one's own country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The main theme of the chapter; it describes the force that unified people and changed borders.
hard.simple_explanation: Deep love for one's own country and the desire for it to be independent.
hard.funny_explanation: Extreme team spirit, but instead of just wearing a hat, you want your team to have its own flag, anthem, and borders.

examples.text: Nationalism emerged as a powerful force in 19th-century Europe.
My dog's nationalism is so strong he barks at any 'foreign' squirrels entering his yard-nation.

hard.real_world_analogy: Nationalism is like that feeling during the Olympics when you jump off the couch because your country's athlete won a medal.

words.meaning: To come out and become known or visible.

medium.simple_explanation: Came out into view or became known for the first time.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you're hiding during hide-and-seek and you finally emerge from the closet covered in dust bunnies.

examples.text: New evidence emerged during the investigation of the mystery.
A very grumpy teenager emerged from the bedroom at noon looking for food.

words.meaning: Large in range and affecting many people.

medium.simple_explanation: Wide-ranging or affecting many things in a big, powerful way.
medium.funny_explanation: Think of a giant broom cleaning a whole dusty floor in one go—it doesn't just fix a tiny spot; it changes everything!

examples.text: The government announced sweeping reforms to the education system.
Mom made sweeping changes to the living room, which basically meant my Xbox was now in the garage.

words.meaning: The act of coming into existence or notice.

medium.simple_explanation: The process of something starting to exist or becoming noticeable.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the slow and slightly scary emergence of a giant pimple right before school photo day.

examples.text: The emergence of the internet changed how the whole world communicates.
The emergence of my dog from the mud puddle was a messy disaster.

words.meaning: Involving people from many different nations.

medium.simple_explanation: Involving or consisting of several different nations or countries.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a school potluck where one kid brings tacos, another brings sushi, and someone else brings pasta—it’s a multi-national feast!

examples.text: The empire was a multi-national state with many different languages spoken.
My backpack is practically multi-national because it has stickers from six different countries.

words.meaning: Relating to a line of rulers from one family.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author contrasts modern nation-states with old empires ruled by powerful families.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to a sequence of rulers from the same family.
hard.funny_explanation: A 'Family Business' where the business is actually an entire country and the 'boss' is always the oldest son.

examples.text: Multi-national dynastic empires were replaced by unified nation-states.
Our TV remote usage is dynastic; my dad rules it, and then my older brother takes over.

hard.real_world_analogy: A dynastic system is like a movie series where the main character is always played by someone from the same family tree.

words.meaning: A general idea or thought about something.

medium.simple_explanation: A general idea or a thought about how something works.
medium.funny_explanation: The concept of 'cleaning your room' seems simple to parents, but to kids, it's a very confusing and mysterious mystery.

examples.text: She struggled to understand the difficult mathematical concept.
The concept of 'waking up early' is something my brain refuses to accept.

words.meaning: Controlled by one single main authority.

medium.simple_explanation: When control or power is kept in one single place or authority.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a kitchen where only Grandma is allowed to touch the stove—all the cooking power is centralised in her hands.

examples.text: The company moved to a centralised system to manage all its orders.
Power in our classroom is centralised in whoever holds the 'talking stick'.

words.meaning: Having complete power over a country or territory.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe a state that has complete and independent authority over its own land.
hard.simple_explanation: Having ultimate power or authority; independent.
hard.funny_explanation: Being the 'Supreme Boss of Everything' in your own house without having to ask the neighbors for permission.

examples.text: A modern state exercises sovereign control over a clearly defined territory.
I am the sovereign ruler of my LEGO castle, and my younger sister needs a visa to enter.

hard.real_world_analogy: Being sovereign is like being the captain of a ship; your word is the final law on that vessel.

words.meaning: An area of land belonging to a country.

medium.simple_explanation: An area of land that belongs to a specific person, group, or country.
medium.funny_explanation: The bottom bunk is my territory, and if you step on it, you’re basically declaring war!

examples.text: The explorers claimed the new territory for their king.
My dog thinks the entire sidewalk is his territory and barks to let everyone know.

words.meaning: People who are legal members of a country.
The characteristics that make someone who they are.

medium.simple_explanation: The characteristics and qualities that make a person or group who they are.
medium.funny_explanation: My identity is basically 50% pizza lover, 40% gamer, and 10% someone who forgets where they put their socks.

examples.text: Speaking their own language helped the group maintain their identity.
The spy had to change his identity, which mostly involved wearing a very fake mustache.

words.meaning: A person's family history or background.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text explains that nationhood is built on shared history or common ancestry.
hard.simple_explanation: The origin or background of a person in terms of family or nationality.
hard.funny_explanation: The long, long line of grandmas and grandpas that lead all the way back to you.

examples.text: The citizens felt united because of their common descent and history.
My cat claims royal descent, but I think he just likes sleeping on expensive pillows.

hard.real_world_analogy: Descent is like a family tree that shows exactly which branches you grew from.

words.meaning: Reaching back beyond the time of memory.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Renan argues that national identity was not always there; it wasn't present from 'time immemorial'.
hard.simple_explanation: Originating in the distant past; very old and reaching beyond memory.
hard.funny_explanation: A time so incredibly old that even your great-great-great-grandpa’s diary doesn't have a record of it.

examples.text: The custom has been practiced in the village since time immemorial.
My dad has been telling the same 'bad joke' since time immemorial—or at least since I was born.

hard.real_world_analogy: Time immemorial is like the 'Once Upon a Time' at the start of a fairy tale that feels like it happened forever ago.

words.meaning: Created or formed with a lot of effort.

medium.simple_explanation: Created or shaped with a lot of effort, often through difficult situations.
medium.funny_explanation: Think of a blacksmith banging on hot metal to make a sword—that's how a strong friendship is forged after surviving a scary math test together.

examples.text: The two nations forged an alliance during the war.
Our bond was forged in the fire of the school cafeteria's mystery meat.

words.meaning: Hard fights or efforts to achieve something.
Including many different types of people or things.

medium.simple_explanation: Including many different types of people or things.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a bag of trail mix—you’ve got nuts, raisins, chocolate chips, and those weird little seeds. It’s very diverse!

examples.text: The city has a diverse population from all over the world.
My excuses for not doing homework are very diverse, ranging from 'the dog ate it' to 'aliens stole it'.

words.meaning: Series of steps taken to achieve a goal.

medium.simple_explanation: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular result.
medium.funny_explanation: The process of getting out of bed involves: five snoozes, a long stare at the wall, and one big groan.

examples.text: The scientific processes were carefully followed during the experiment.
The process of making a sandwich usually ends with me just eating the cheese by itself.

words.meaning: Gave a speech or a lecture to others.
Someone who thinks deeply about life and ideas.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to Ernst Renan, who used logic and deep thinking to define what a nation is.
hard.simple_explanation: A person who studies the fundamental nature of knowledge, reality, and existence.
hard.funny_explanation: Someone whose actual job is to sit in a comfy chair, stare at the ceiling, and ask 'But... why?' about everything.

examples.text: The French philosopher Ernst Renan gave a famous lecture on the meaning of a nation.
My 5-year-old cousin is a philosopher because he keeps asking why the sky is blue and why broccoli exists.

hard.real_world_analogy: A philosopher is like a detective, but instead of solving crimes, they try to solve the mysteries of 'Why do humans do what they do?'

words.meaning: Described the main ideas of something simply.

medium.simple_explanation: Gave a summary of the main points or the general shape of an idea.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you tell your friend about a movie and only give them the 'cool parts' without explaining every single boring detail.

examples.text: The coach outlined the strategy for the upcoming game.
I outlined my plan to get more snacks, but it mostly just involved looking sad near the kitchen.

words.meaning: Happening at a time after something else.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to show the sequence of events: first the lecture was given, and then it was published.
hard.simple_explanation: Happening after something else has happened.
hard.funny_explanation: The fancy way of saying 'and then...' after something usually went wrong or changed.

examples.text: The lecture was subsequently published as a famous essay.
I ate ten spicy tacos and subsequently drank three gallons of water.

hard.real_world_analogy: Subseequently is like the next scene in a movie after a 'Two Hours Later' sign appears.

words.meaning: Having a specific name or title.

medium.simple_explanation: Given a specific name or title.
medium.funny_explanation: If I write a book about my cat, it will be entitled 'The Furry Overlord: Why I am Never Allowed to Sleep'.

examples.text: He wrote a famous essay entitled 'The Future of Humanity'.
I feel entitled to a nap after doing exactly five minutes of studying.

words.meaning: Points out what is wrong with something.

medium.simple_explanation: Points out the faults or mistakes in something in a serious way.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when your older sister criticises your outfit and tells you that socks with sandals is a crime against humanity.

examples.text: The reviewer criticises the movie for having a very boring plot.
The food critic criticises the soup for being 'wetter than water,' which doesn't even make sense.

words.meaning: An idea, belief, or opinion about something.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Renan uses this word when challenging the common belief or 'notion' of what makes a nation.
hard.simple_explanation: A conception of or belief about something.
hard.funny_explanation: A brain-spark or a 'hunch' that you think is true, like the notion that eating crust makes your hair curly.

examples.text: Renan criticized the notion that a nation is formed only by a common language.
I have a notion that my dog understands English but just chooses to ignore me.

hard.real_world_analogy: A notion is like a sketch of a drawing—it’s an idea of how things are, but it might not be the final picture.

words.meaning: The highest point or the end of something.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Renan describes a nation as the final result or peak of a long history of sacrifice.
hard.simple_explanation: The highest or most important point of something, especially reached after a long time.
hard.funny_explanation: The big, loud 'Ta-da!' moment at the end of a very long magic trick.

examples.text: The festival was the culmination of months of hard work by the students.
Winning the video game was the culmination of a week spent eating snacks and not doing homework.

hard.real_world_analogy: A culmination is like the very last piece of a 1,000-piece puzzle that finally shows the whole picture.

words.meaning: Serious and hard efforts to do something.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It highlights the serious, determined efforts people made to build their nations.
hard.simple_explanation: An attempt to achieve a goal; hard work or effort.
hard.funny_explanation: Trying really, really hard to do something difficult, like trying to lick your own elbow.

examples.text: A nation is the result of long past endeavours and sacrifices.
Despite my best endeavours, I still cannot find where I hid my own birthday presents.

hard.real_world_analogy: Endeavours are like the hundreds of tiny steps you take while climbing a very steep hill.

words.meaning: Giving up something important for a good cause.
Great love and loyalty for a person or cause.

medium.simple_explanation: Great love, loyalty, or enthusiasm for a person, activity, or cause.
medium.funny_explanation: My level of devotion to this specific brand of potato chips is so high, I’d probably travel across the country for one bag.

examples.text: The nurse showed great devotion to her patients.
His devotion to sleeping in on Saturdays is truly inspiring.

words.meaning: Showing extreme courage like a hero.
Great honor and praise given to someone.
Extremely important and necessary.

medium.simple_explanation: Something that is absolutely necessary or extremely important.
medium.funny_explanation: Wi-Fi is an essential ingredient for my survival, right next to oxygen and snacks.

examples.text: Water is essential for all living things to survive.
It is essential that you don't touch my fries if you want to remain my friend.

words.meaning: Support by one person or group for another.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Renan defines a nation as a 'large-scale solidarity,' meaning people standing together.
hard.simple_explanation: Unity or agreement of feeling or action, especially among individuals with a common interest.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'we're all in this together' vibe, like when a whole class agrees to stay silent so everyone gets an early recess.

examples.text: The workers showed solidarity by going on strike together for better wages.
In a show of solidarity, all my friends wore silly hats to my birthday party.

hard.real_world_analogy: Solidarity is like a group of people holding hands to form a circle—if one lets go, the circle breaks, but together they are strong.

words.meaning: A direct vote by all people on an issue.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Renan uses this metaphor to say that a nation exists because its people 'vote' to be part of it every day.
hard.simple_explanation: A direct vote by all the people of a region to decide on an important issue.
hard.funny_explanation: When the teacher lets the whole class vote: 'Should we have a quiz today, Yes or No?' and everyone’s vote actually counts.

examples.text: The region decided to join the neighboring country after a fair plebiscite.
We held a family plebiscite to decide if the new puppy should be named 'Bacon' or 'Sir Fluff-a-lot'.

hard.real_world_analogy: A plebiscite is like a giant 'thumbs up' or 'thumbs down' from every single person in a room to make a final choice.

words.meaning: Taking control of a territory by force.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe how a nation should not forcefully take over another territory against its will.
hard.simple_explanation: Adding a territory to one's own territory by appropriation.
hard.funny_explanation: When your older brother slowly moves his pile of laundry until it 'accidentally' takes over your side of the room.

examples.text: The powerful country was criticized for annexing the smaller neighbor's land.
My cat is slowly annexing the sofa by leaving more fur on it every single day.

hard.real_world_analogy: Annexing is like a school bully deciding that your desk now belongs to them just because they sat there.

words.meaning: A promise that something will certainly happen.

medium.simple_explanation: A formal promise that something will be done or will happen.
medium.funny_explanation: There is a 100% guarantee that if I drop a piece of toast, it will land butter-side down on the rug.

examples.text: The shop gave a one-year guarantee on the new television.
I can guarantee that I will be hungry again ten minutes after finishing dinner.

words.meaning: The freedom to live as you choose.

medium.simple_explanation: The state of being free within society from oppressive restrictions.
medium.funny_explanation: Liberty is the freedom to choose your own toppings on a pizza without your little brother complaining.

examples.text: The people fought hard to regain their liberty after years of rule.
I took the liberty of eating the last cookie because nobody's name was on it.

words.meaning: Features or qualities that belong to someone.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The question asks the reader to list the qualities or features that Renan believes make up a nation.
hard.simple_explanation: Qualities or features that are characteristic of someone or something.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'ingredients' that make you who you are—like 'funny,' 'tall,' or 'great at eating pizza.'

examples.text: Honesty and bravery are important attributes of a good leader.
The main attributes of my dog are a wet nose and a tail that never stops wagging.

hard.real_world_analogy: Attributes are like the specs of a phone—the camera quality, the screen size, and the battery life define what that phone is.

words.meaning: Love and pride for one's own country.

medium.simple_explanation: A strong feeling of love, pride, and belonging to one's own country.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like being a super-fan of your country, wearing its jersey and cheering until your voice is gone.

examples.text: The French Revolution sparked a new sense of nationalism among the citizens.
His nationalism was so strong he tried to convince everyone that his country invented the internet and pizza.

words.meaning: A way of showing thoughts or feelings.
A sudden change in government by the people.

medium.simple_explanation: A sudden and complete change in a government, usually by force.
medium.funny_explanation: When the citizens decide the King’s 'Free Pizza Fridays' aren't enough and fire him entirely.

examples.text: The French Revolution changed how the country was governed forever.
There was a revolution in the cafeteria when they replaced fries with kale chips.

words.meaning: Completely developed or having full status.

medium.simple_explanation: Completely developed and having all the necessary parts or features.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a baby bird finally growing all its feathers and realizing it can actually fly now.

examples.text: France was a full-fledged kingdom before the revolution started.
After finding a nickel on the ground, Timmy considered himself a full-fledged billionaire.

words.meaning: Related to a specific area of land.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to a specific area of land that is owned or controlled.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a cat that gets mad if you sit in its favorite spot because it 'owns' that square foot of carpet.

examples.text: France was a territorial state with clearly defined borders.
The dog was very territorial about the squeaky toy and wouldn't let the cat near it.

words.meaning: Having total power without any limits.

medium.simple_explanation: Total and complete, with no limits on power.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a TV remote owner who refuses to let anyone else even look at the buttons.

examples.text: France was ruled by an absolute monarch who made all the decisions.
The cat has absolute control over who gets to use the sofa.

words.meaning: A king or queen who rules a country.
Related to a set of laws for a country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this to describe the legal shift from a king's whim to a formal system of laws following the French Revolution.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to a set of fundamental rules that govern a country.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate 'Rule Book' for a country, like the manual for a LEGO set that tells you exactly where every piece must go so the whole thing doesn't fall apart.

examples.text: The revolution brought about major constitutional changes in France.
My cat thinks he has a constitutional right to sleep on my face at 3 AM.

hard.real_world_analogy: A board game's official rulebook that prevents players from just making up moves as they go.

words.meaning: The power of a country to rule itself.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To explain the transition of power from a single monarch to the collective body of citizens.
hard.simple_explanation: The supreme power or authority of a state to govern itself.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like being the absolute boss of your own bedroom where you decide what posters go up and no one can tell you otherwise.

examples.text: The revolution transferred sovereignty from the king to the people.
I declared sovereignty over the last slice of pizza, making me the ultimate ruler of the dinner table.

hard.real_world_analogy: The captain of a ship who has the final say on which direction the vessel travels.

words.meaning: A system of government ruled by a king.

medium.simple_explanation: A type of government where a King or Queen is the head of the country.
medium.funny_explanation: A system where 'Because I'm the King' is the only reason you need for everything.

examples.text: The revolution took power away from the monarchy and gave it to the citizens.
I tried to start a monarchy in my bedroom, but my mom still made me clean it.

words.meaning: Announced something publicly and officially.

medium.simple_explanation: Announced something officially and loudly for everyone to hear.
medium.funny_explanation: Like standing on a cafeteria table and shouting 'I AM THE BEST AT DODGEBALL!'

examples.text: The revolution proclaimed that the people should control the nation.
The toddler proclaimed that it was officially 'No Nap Day' in the house.

words.meaning: From this time forward.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to signal a permanent change in the status of the French people from the moment of the revolution.
hard.simple_explanation: From this time forward.
hard.funny_explanation: A fancy way of saying 'starting right now and forever,' usually used when you're trying to sound like a very serious wizard.

examples.text: The people would henceforth shape the destiny of the nation.
Henceforth, I shall only eat my sandwiches cut into the shape of dinosaurs!

hard.real_world_analogy: A New Year's resolution that you actually intend to keep for the rest of the year.

words.meaning: To form or be part of a whole.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe how the citizens themselves are the building blocks that form a nation.
hard.simple_explanation: To be the parts that form or make up a whole.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s like how flour, sugar, and eggs join forces to 'constitute' a delicious cake.

examples.text: The citizens were the ones who would constitute the new nation.
Does eating five different kinds of cheese constitute a balanced breakfast? I hope so!

hard.real_world_analogy: The individual players who come together to form a football team.

words.meaning: What is planned to happen in the future.
People who take part in a revolution.

medium.simple_explanation: People who take part in or support a sudden change in government.
medium.funny_explanation: The group of kids who decide the school lunch is so bad they’re going to rewrite the entire menu.

examples.text: French revolutionaries worked together to change the laws of their country.
The revolutionaries in the back of the bus demanded more stops at the ice cream shop.

words.meaning: Shared by every member of a group.

medium.simple_explanation: Something shared or done by every member of a group.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a group project where everyone actually does the work for once.

examples.text: The people developed a collective identity as citizens of France.
The class made a collective decision to stare at the clock until it was time for recess.

words.meaning: Who or what a person or group is.
A French word meaning fatherland.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The book introduces this French term to show how the revolutionaries promoted the idea of a shared homeland.
hard.simple_explanation: A French word meaning 'the fatherland' or homeland.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like giving your country a big, warm hug and calling it 'Dad' to show how much you love it.

examples.text: The idea of la patrie emphasized the notion of a united community.
He saluted his backyard and called it 'la patrie' of the Squirrel Empire.

hard.real_world_analogy: The feeling of pride you have for your home town or your favorite local sports team.

words.meaning: A French word meaning citizen.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Introduced as a revolutionary concept that replaced 'subjects' with 'citizens' who have equal rights.

hard.funny_explanation: Before the revolution, people were just 'subjects' (basically the king's fans), but 'citoyen' turned everyone into an official member of the club with a vote.

examples.text: The concept of le citoyen gave everyone equal rights under the law.
I am a 'citoyen' of the Internet, and my duty is to look at funny cat videos.

hard.real_world_analogy: Moving from being a guest at a party to being one of the hosts who helps decide the music.

words.meaning: A belief or an idea about something.

medium.simple_explanation: An idea, belief, or understanding about something.
medium.funny_explanation: The silly notion that my dog actually understands the plot of the movie we're watching.

examples.text: They promoted the notion of a united community with equal rights.
He had a weird notion that if he ate enough carrots, he would grow bunny ears.

words.meaning: Joined together for a common purpose.
An official flag or symbol.

medium.simple_explanation: A flag or banner used to represent a leader or a group.
medium.funny_explanation: A very fancy, old-school flag that says 'I'm the boss' without using any words.

examples.text: The tricolour flag replaced the old royal standard.
The knight carried his royal standard so high he accidentally hit a low tree branch.

words.meaning: Chosen by voting for a position.
A group of people gathered for a purpose.

medium.funny_explanation: Like a school assembly, but instead of learning about fire safety, they’re deciding the fate of a nation.

examples.text: The National Assembly was formed to represent the citizens.
The secret assembly of squirrels met to discuss the storage of winter acorns.

words.meaning: Religious or official songs of praise.

medium.simple_explanation: Songs of praise or loyalty, often for a country or religion.
medium.funny_explanation: Songs that everyone sings loudly, even the people who can't hit a single note.

examples.text: New hymns were composed to celebrate the birth of the nation.
We sang national hymns so loud that the neighbor's cat ran away.

words.meaning: Solemn promises to tell the truth.

medium.simple_explanation: Serious and formal promises to tell the truth or be loyal.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a 'pinky swear,' but with much more serious costumes and a lot more at stake.

examples.text: The citizens took oaths of loyalty to the new constitution.
My sister and I took secret oaths never to tell who actually ate the last cookie.

words.meaning: People who die for their beliefs.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the people who died for the cause of the nation and were honored to build a sense of unity.
hard.simple_explanation: People who suffer or die for their beliefs or a cause.
hard.funny_explanation: While usually very serious, you might call your friend a martyr because they missed the school trip just to finish a group project for the team.

examples.text: The nation took oaths and remembered its martyrs to build national pride.
My brother thinks he’s a martyr because he had to do the dishes while everyone else watched the movie.

hard.real_world_analogy: A person who takes the blame for a prank so the rest of the class doesn't get punished.

words.meaning: Honored the memory of a person or event.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe how the memory of heroes was kept alive to foster a sense of national identity.
hard.simple_explanation: To preserve the memory of an event or person by a celebration or ceremony.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like throwing a giant 'Remember How Awesome This Was?' party every single year.

examples.text: The soldiers who fell in battle were commemorated with a grand statue.
We commemorated the day I finally beat my dad at chess by ordering three pizzas.

hard.real_world_analogy: Anniversary celebrations or holidays like Independence Day.

words.meaning: Managed by a single main authority.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the new way the French government was organized to have power in one main location.
hard.simple_explanation: Concentrating control or power in a single place or person.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine if there was only one TV remote in the world that controlled every television on Earth. That would be very centralised (and very messy!).

examples.text: A centralised administrative system was put in place to manage the whole country.
I tried to create a centralised snack storage system, but I ended up eating everything in five minutes.

hard.real_world_analogy: A spider sitting in the middle of a web, controlling every single thread from one spot.

words.meaning: Related to managing a government or business.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the systems and tasks related to managing the country's laws and services.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to the management or organization of a system.
hard.funny_explanation: The boring stuff behind the scenes, like filling out forms and organizing files, that makes sure the big stuff actually works.

examples.text: The new government simplified administrative tasks to make things run smoothly.
My administrative duties at home include making sure the dog is fed and the remote isn't lost.

hard.real_world_analogy: The school office staff who handle the paperwork so that teachers can focus on teaching.

words.meaning: Created or prepared something systematically.

medium.simple_explanation: To create or develop a plan or a set of rules carefully.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a mad scientist coming up with the perfect recipe for a giant slime monster.

examples.text: The government formulated new laws that applied to everyone.
I formulated a plan to get my homework done in five minutes, but it involved a lot of luck.

words.meaning: Remaining the same in all cases.
An area of land under one ruler.

medium.simple_explanation: An area of land that belongs to a specific person, group, or country.
medium.funny_explanation: The specific part of the couch that you have claimed as your own 'No Siblings Allowed' zone.

examples.text: Laws were made uniform for all citizens within the French territory.
The cat guarded its territory—the laundry basket—against any invading socks.

words.meaning: Taxes paid on goods coming into a country.

medium.simple_explanation: Taxes paid to the government when goods are moved into or out of a region.
medium.funny_explanation: When the government acts like a big brother who takes a bite of your sandwich just because you walked into the kitchen.

examples.text: The revolutionaries abolished internal customs duties to make trade easier.
I had to pay a 'customs fee' of two gummy bears to my brother to cross the hallway.

words.meaning: Formally put an end to a system.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To explain that the old, unfair taxes and customs were completely removed by the revolutionaries.
hard.simple_explanation: To officially end or stop a law, system, or institution.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like having a rule that you can't wear hats, and then the Principal says 'No more of that!' and throws the rule in the trash forever.

examples.text: Customs duties and internal dues were abolished to help trade.
I wish they would abolish the rule that says I have to clean my room on Saturdays.

hard.real_world_analogy: A teacher canceling homework for the rest of the semester.

words.meaning: Money that a person is required to pay.
Started to use or follow something new.
Relating to a specific part of a country.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to a particular area or part of a country.
medium.funny_explanation: Like how people in one city call it 'soda' and people in another call it 'pop.'

examples.text: Regional dialects were discouraged to create a common national language.
Our regional tradition involves wearing silly hats every third Tuesday of the month.

words.meaning: Local forms of a language.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author notes how regional versions of language were discouraged to create a unified national language.
hard.simple_explanation: Different versions of a language spoken in specific regions.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s like how some people say 'soda,' some say 'pop,' and some say 'fizzy drink,' even though they are all talking about the same sugary water.

examples.text: While many dialects were spoken, Paris French became the standard language.
My family has a weird dialect where 'get that thing' means 'pass the salt.'

hard.real_world_analogy: Different accents and slang used by people from different parts of the same country.

words.meaning: Tried to prevent something from happening.
An important task or goal.
To set someone free from control.

medium.simple_explanation: To set someone or something free from being controlled by others.
medium.funny_explanation: Sneaking into the pantry to 'liberate' the cookies from their jar.

examples.text: The French army aimed to liberate other European nations from their rulers.
I finally decided to liberate my old toys from the dusty box in the attic.

words.meaning: Rule by a leader with absolute power.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the absolute and often unfair power of kings that the French aimed to end across Europe.
hard.simple_explanation: The exercise of absolute power in a cruel or oppressive way.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a king who makes a law that everyone must hop on one foot every Tuesday just because he thinks it's funny. That's despotism.

examples.text: The French mission was to liberate Europe from the grip of despotism.
My older sister's rule over the TV remote is a clear case of despotism.

hard.real_world_analogy: A school bully who dictates who can play on the swings and who can't.

words.meaning: Having a high level of knowledge.
Planned activities to achieve a goal.

medium.funny_explanation: My month-long campaign to convince my parents that I absolutely need a new gaming console.

examples.text: Their military campaigns helped spread the idea of nationalism across Europe.

words.meaning: The sudden start of something unpleasant.

medium.simple_explanation: The sudden start of something, like a war or a disease.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the sudden outbreak of giggles in a quiet classroom during a boring movie.

examples.text: The outbreak of revolutionary wars spread French ideas to other countries.
There was a sudden outbreak of dancing when the lunchroom started playing music.

words.meaning: In or to a foreign country.

hard.simple_explanation: An annual calendar or handbook containing information on many subjects.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a yearly 'Cheat Sheet' for life, telling you when the moon will be full and which days are best for planting potatoes.

examples.text: The German almanac's cover used powerful images to spark the idea of freedom.
According to my imaginary almanac, today is the perfect day for a nap.

hard.real_world_analogy: A diary combined with a weather forecast and a fact-book.

words.meaning: A person who writes for newspapers.
Attacked a place suddenly and forcefully.

medium.simple_explanation: Attacked a place by rushing into it suddenly and with great force.
medium.funny_explanation: How students storm the cafeteria when they hear it’s 'Taco Tuesday.'

examples.text: The crowd stormed the Bastille to show they were fighting against the king.
The puppies stormed the kitchen as soon as they heard the kibble hit the bowl.

words.meaning: A strong building used for defense.

medium.simple_explanation: A strong building or a group of buildings built to be easily defended.
medium.funny_explanation: The pillow fort in the living room that is 100% dragon-proof and sibling-resistant.
